Archive item 1: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
Source format: personal journal

2023-10-18
Rained all morning. Good, the ground needed it. Found a small leak in the laundry room ceiling, right corner near the vent. Dripping into a bucket now. Could be the roof, could be the vent pipe flashing. Called a roofer, guy named Mike from Apex Roofing. He's coming Friday to take a look. Need to clear the stuff out from under the window in the laundry room so he can get to it. Also, the leak is right above the water heater. Hope that's not a problem.

2023-10-19
Still overcast. Called the insurance agent about the roof leak. She said get a roofer's report first, then call her back. She gave me the claim number to jot down: CLM-2023-4471. Told me to take photos of the stain and the bucket. Did that. Also took a photo of the ceiling around the stain. The bucket is at 2 inches of water after 24 hours. Not a gusher, but steady.

- Photos on phone in folder "leak Oct 2023".
- Claim number CLM-2023-4471.
- Mike from Apex coming Fri 10/21, 9:30 AM.

2023-10-20
Cleared the laundry room. Moved the dryer vent hose so there's a path. Also put an old towel down to catch drips when I empty the bucket. Paid the water bill online. Confirmation #88421. The leak is still dripping. Called Mike to confirm tomorrow. He said he'd bring his ladder and a moisture meter.

2023-10-21
Mike came at 9:30 sharp. Went up on the roof. Found the problem – the boot around the vent pipe is cracked and the flashing is pulled up about an inch on the north side. He said it's an easy fix, maybe $350 for parts and labor. He sealed it temporarily with some caulk to stop the leak for now. Took photos of the boot and flashing. He'll email me a formal estimate Monday. The bucket hasn't caught a drop since he left, so fingers crossed.

- Mike's estimate due via email ~10/24.
- Temporary seal should hold until then.

Delgado Residence street address 4102 Mockingbird Lane. Record status: current.

2023-10-22
Sunny and cool. The leak is dry. Put the laundry room back together except for the bucket, which I'll leave until the real fix is done. Went to HEB, got the WD-40. Fixed the back gate hinge. Quiet now. Also bought a new pack of rags. Need to call the insurance agent Monday with Mike's estimate. She wanted the roofer's report before we talk about coverage.

2023-10-23
Monday. Mike's email came in at 8:15 AM. Estimate is $380 total: $150 for the boot, $150 for flashing repair, $80 for labor. Itemized, looks fine. Called the insurance agent, left a voicemail with the estimate amount and the claim number. She said she'd call back after she reviews it. Also, the neighborhood fall cleanup is Nov 4. Checked the flyer – they do take latex paint, but not oil. Good, the shed cans are latex. Will drop them off.

2023-10-24
Agent called back. She said the claim is open, and since the damage is from a storm (there was a hail storm back in April, remember?), it might be covered. She needs the photos and the estimate. Sent them via email. She said a claims adjuster might need to come out to verify the damage. Waiting to hear. Also, the bucket is still dry. Mike's temporary fix is holding well.

- Photos sent to agent 10/24.
- Awaiting adjuster visit.

2023-10-25
No word from the adjuster yet. Called the agent, she said they're backed up but should schedule within a week. Fine. Meanwhile, the weather is nice. Raked the back yard today. Got 4 more bags. Put them behind the fence with the others. That's 10 total now. Monday pickup should handle it.

2023-10-26
Thought I heard dripping in the laundry room, but it was just the water heater cycling. The ceiling stain is dry. Touched it – no dampness. Good. Spent some time cleaning the garage. Found the old paint cans – 3 cans of latex, all sealed. Good to go for Nov 4. Also found an old box of holiday decorations from last year. Noted to go through it before the season starts.
- Photos sent to agent 11:15 AM.
- New claim opened, linked to April claim.
- Wait for adjuster call.

2024-02-04
Sunday. No call from the adjuster yet. The agent did email back at 3:10 PM confirming she received the photos and the claim is in the system. She said the adjuster is scheduled for tomorrow or Tuesday, depending on the storm backlog. Noted. Meanwhile, went outside and inspected the shed more closely. The dent is about the size of my fist, on the lower back corner, and it looks like the paint chipped around the dent. Will need to patch that to prevent rust. Also checked the gutters – one seam on the front corner looks like it might be separating. Not sure if that's from the hail or just old age. Took a photo anyway and added it to the claim notes. The fence picket is still on the ground. Will pick it up before mowing. The weather is sunny and cold today, in the 40s. Good day to stay inside.

- Check gutters – front seam, possible separation.
- Shed dent: fist-sized, paint chipped.
- Fence picket still down.

Storm Date event date 2024-02-03. Record status: current.

2024-02-05
Monday. Adjuster called at 8:50 AM. A man named David, he said he'd be out this afternoon between 1 and 4. I said fine. He asked about the April leak and whether the roof boot was repaired. I told him yes, Mike fixed it in October, and I have the receipt. He said to have it ready. He also asked about the shed. I told him about the dent and the chipped paint. He said he'd look at it. While waiting, I swept the hail off the back patio – there was still a pile in the corner. Also picked up the fence picket and leaned it against the garage. At 1:20 PM David arrived. He walked around the house, took a lot of photos. He climbed up on the roof with a ladder he had in his truck. He was up there maybe 20 minutes. He said the roof shingles have some granule loss in a few spots, and a couple of shingles on the south slope look like they might have been lifted by the wind. He said the AC fins are definitely dented and he'd note that. He looked at the shed and said the dent is minor but the paint chip needs sealing to avoid rust. He also looked at the gutter seam and said it might be from the hail, but he'd need to check if the seam was already weak. He said he'd write up the report tonight and send it to the agent tomorrow. I gave him Mike's receipt for the boot repair. He said that would help with the April claim. He left at 2:40 PM. I felt good about it, but I'll wait for the report.

- Adjuster visit done 2/5, report expected 2/6.
- Roof: granule loss, possible shingle lift.
- AC fins dented.
- Shed dent minor, paint chip.
- Gutter seam questionable.

2024-02-06
Tuesday. No report yet. Checked email at 9:00 AM – nothing. Called the agent at 10:15 AM. She said David's report is still being written and should be in by the end of the day. She said I'd get a copy by email. Fine. Meanwhile, I went to the hardware store and got a small can of rust-preventive paint for the shed dent. It's the same color as the shed, or close enough. Will patch it tomorrow when the weather is dry. Also picked up a new nail for the fence picket. Might just reattach it myself instead of waiting. The weather is clear and cold. Good day for errands. Checked the laundry room bucket one more time – still dry. The boot fix is solid. Noted to follow up on the report tomorrow if I don't hear back by 5 PM.

- Follow up on report if no email by 5 PM 2/7.
- Shed paint patch planned for 2/7.
The report says the hail size he used in his assessment was 2.75 inch max. That matches what I remember from the storm – it was the biggest I've seen in the 12 years I've lived here. The report lists it as the storm's max hail size. Good to have that in writing.

I called the agent at 4:00 PM to confirm she got it. She said yes, and that she'd file the claim with the ins. company tomorrow morning. She said the claim number would be assigned within a day or two. She also said I should get quotes from contractors for the roof work, but to wait for the ins. adjuster's estimate before signing anything. Noted.

- Report received 2/7, 47 photos.
- Hail size max 2.75 inch in storm description.
- Claim to be filed 2/8.
- Get contractor quotes, but don't sign until ins. estimate arrives.

2024-02-08
Thursday. The agent called at 11:00 AM. Claim filed. Claim number: CLM-2024-01874. She read it to me over the phone and said I'd get an email confirmation too. She said the ins. company will assign their own adjuster to do a damage assessment. That could take a week or more, depending on how busy they are. She said to expect a call from them to schedule a visit. I wrote the claim number on a sticky note and put it on the fridge.

After lunch I called three roofing companies for estimates. First one, Peak Roofing, said they could come out next Tuesday. Second one, Summit Exteriors, said Thursday. Third one, Blue Ridge Roofing, said they'd have to check their schedule and call me back. I left my number. I'll give them until Monday.

Also called an HVAC place about the AC fins. The guy I talked to, Ron, said they do free estimates for hail damage. He said he could come by Monday afternoon. I scheduled it for 1:00 PM. He said to have the adjuster's report handy. I'll print a copy.

The shed paint is dry. Looks fine. Not perfect, but it'll keep the rust from starting. I'll touch it up again in the spring.

Storm Date hail size max 2.75 inch. Record status: current.

- Claim # CLM-2024-01874
- Peak Roofing – Tue
- Summit Exteriors – Thu
- HVAC (Ron) – Mon 1:00 PM
- Blue Ridge Roofing – call back pending

2024-02-09
Friday. No call from Blue Ridge yet. I'll try them again Monday.

The ins. company's adjuster called at 10:00 AM. Her name is Patricia Okafor. She said she handles the northern part of the county. She asked if she could come out next Wednesday, Feb 14, in the morning. I said yes. She said she'd be here between 9 and 11. She asked me to have any receipts for temporary repairs ready. I mentioned the boot repair and the shed paint. She said to keep the receipts for the paint too, since it's a preventive measure. Good. I have both.

She also asked if I had any photos of the storm damage from the day of. I said yes, I took some on my phone while David was here. She said to email them to her before the visit. I'll do that tonight.

After the call, I went to the bank to deposit a check from my sister. Not related to the claim, just life. While I was there, I noticed the ATM receipt printed wrong – it was missing the last two digits of the deposit amount. I went inside and the teller fixed it. Not a big deal, but I like to keep my records straight.

- Ins. adjuster visit: Wed 2/14, 9-11 AM.
- Email photos to P. Okafor before then.
- Keep receipts for boot repair and shed paint.

2024-02-10
Saturday. Cold but sunny. I spent the morning going through my photos from the storm and picking the best ones for Patricia. I sent her 12 photos by email at 11:30 AM. I wrote a short note explaining what each one showed – the roof from the street, the dented AC fins, the shed, the gutter seam, and a couple of the hail itself on the patio before I swept it. She replied within the hour, said she got them and they'd help.
I showed her the folder with the receipts. She looked at the boot repair and the shed paint. She said both were reasonable temporary repairs. She asked if I had a receipt for the tarp from the first night. I said no, I bought it at the hardware store and paid cash, didn't think to keep the receipt. She said that's fine, she can note it as an expense if I can find any record. I'll check my bank statement; I might have used my debit card. I thought I paid cash, but I'm not sure now.

She said the dented AC fins are "cosmetic" but she'll include them in the report anyway. She said the gutter seam at the corner of the garage is a separate issue from the hail, and the adjuster's report will note it as "pre-existing wear." I didn't argue. She said the final report should be ready in 5 to 7 business days. She'll email me a copy.

I sent her a thank-you email after she left. She replied right away, said to call her if I have questions.

- P. Okafor – visit done. Report expected in 5-7 business days.
- Check bank statement for tarp purchase.

2024-02-15
Thursday. Summit Exteriors came by at 10:00. Two guys, one older and one younger. The older one, Mike, did most of the talking. He walked the roof, took measurements, looked at the attic from the hatch in the hallway. He said the ventilation looks fine, which is good. He said the shingles are at the end of their life and the hail damage is "moderate." He quoted me $9,400 for a full tear-off and replacement with architectural shingles. He said that includes new underlayment and ice and water shield at the eaves. He left me a printed estimate with a line-item breakdown.

I asked about a metal roof. He said they don't do metal, they're strictly asphalt. He said if I want a metal roof, I should call a different company. Fine.

He said they're booking about 3 weeks out. If I decide to go with them, they need a 20% deposit to hold the date. I told him I'm still waiting on the insurance report, so I can't decide anything yet. He said no problem, the estimate is good for 90 days.

Maya R. Delgado's email address is maya.delgado@example.com. Record status: current.

- Summit Exteriors – estimate $9,400. Good for 90 days.
- Still waiting on Blue Ridge call-back.

2024-02-16
Friday. No call from Blue Ridge. I'm starting to think they don't want the job. I called them again this afternoon. The same woman answered. She said Dale is out sick and will call me Monday. We'll see.

I also checked my bank statement online for the tarp. Turns out I did use my debit card. The transaction is there, $24.37 at the hardware store on Feb 3. I printed the statement page and added it to the folder. I'll email that to Patricia too, just to be thorough.

I spent the evening looking at the Summit estimate. The line items make sense. The price is a little higher than I hoped, but not crazy. I called Peak Roofing to confirm their visit for Tuesday. The woman who answered said they'll be here between 9 and 12. She asked if I had a chance to look at their website. I said no. She said they have photos of recent jobs. I said I'd look.

- Blue Ridge – Dale out sick, call Monday.
- Tarp receipt found – sent to P. Okafor.
- Peak Roofing – Tue 2/20, 9-12.

2024-02-17
Saturday. Cold and windy. I didn't do much. I looked at Peak's website. Their photos look good. They have a few jobs in the area. I saw one that matched my roof style. I'll ask about it on Tuesday.

I also looked at the Summit estimate again. The line items are:
- Tear-off and haul-away: $2,100
- New underlayment: $900
- Ice and water shield (eaves and valleys): $600
- Architectural shingles (30-year): $3,800
- Ridge vent and caps: $500
- Labor: $1,500
- Total: $9,400
2024-04-01
Monday. Rain this morning, cleared by noon. Dale from Blue Ridge called at 9:15 to confirm. He said they can start on the 8th, weather permitting. I told him the check from the insurance company came in the mail on Saturday. He said they'll need the deposit before they order materials, so I should drop it off this week. I said I'd bring it by Wednesday.

Called Patricia Okafor this afternoon to tell her the check arrived. She said good, and that she'd already sent the final report to the carrier. She asked if I had the contractor's certificate of insurance. I said I'd get it from Dale. She said to email it to her once I have it, so she can close the file.

- Blue Ridge start date: Mon 4/8, weather permitting
- Deposit due before materials order
- Need COI from Dale → email to P. Okafor

2024-04-02
Tuesday. Sunny, cool. Went to Blue Ridge's office after work. Dale wasn't there, but the receptionist took my deposit check. She gave me a receipt and a copy of their certificate of insurance. I looked at it in the car—it's current through October. I emailed the PDF to Patricia when I got home.

Also stopped at the bank to deposit the insurance check. The teller asked if I wanted it held. I said no, just deposit it. It should clear in a couple days. I'll pay the rest of the balance when the work is done.

- Deposit paid: $1,880 (20% of $9,400)
- COI emailed to P. Okafor
- Insurance check deposited

2024-04-03
Wednesday. Windy. Dale called to say the shingles are in stock and they'll deliver them Friday. He said they'll do the tear-off on Monday, then the underlayment and ice and water shield on Tuesday, and the shingles Wednesday and Thursday. He said the ridge vent gets done on Friday. That's if the weather holds.

I asked about the old skylight. He said they'll frame it out and patch the decking, but they won't install a new one. I said that's fine, I don't need one. He said the patch will be covered by the new shingles and you won't be able to tell it was there.

- Shingle delivery: Fri 4/5
- Tear-off: Mon 4/8
- Underlayment + ice/water: Tue 4/9
- Shingles: Wed 4/10 – Thu 4/11
- Ridge vent: Fri 4/12

2024-04-04
Thursday. Warm for April. I cleared the driveway and moved the car to the street. I also took down the wind chimes by the front door so they don't get in the way. The tarp is still on the roof from February. Dale said they'll take it down when they start the tear-off.

I looked at my folder to make sure I have everything. I have the original estimate, the signed contract, the deposit receipt, the COI, and the insurance paperwork. Patricia said the adjuster's report is final, so I don't need to worry about that anymore.

The neighbor across the street, Mr. Chen, came over to ask about the noise. I told him the roof work starts Monday. He said he'd let his wife know. He asked how long it would take. I said about a week, maybe a little more if it rains.

2024-04-05
Friday. Overcast. The shingles were delivered this morning. Two pallets in the driveway, wrapped in plastic. Dale came by with the delivery to check the order. He said everything looks right. He also brought the dump trailer and parked it in the driveway, so the old shingles will go straight in.

I asked him about the weather for Monday. He said the forecast is clear, so they'll start at 7:30. He said they'll be done with the tear-off by the end of the day, unless they hit plywood that needs replacing. He said he'd call me if that happens.

- Shingles delivered
- Dump trailer in driveway
- Start time: Mon 7:30 AM

2024-04-06
Saturday. Nice day. I stayed home in case anyone came by. Nobody did. I looked at the pallets from the window. They're still wrapped. I read the contract again to check the payment schedule. It says the balance is due upon completion. Good.
2024-05-01
Wednesday. Rain off and on all day. The roof is done and I'm still getting used to how quiet the house is without the tarp flapping. Dale came by this morning to pick up the last check. I had it ready. He walked around the house first, checked the ridge vent and the flashing around the chimney, then said everything looked good. I gave him the final payment of $4,150.00. He said the warranty paperwork will be mailed to me within a week. I put the receipt in the folder.

2024-05-02
Thursday. Clear. I finally took the wind chimes back out and hung them by the front door. Also swept the driveway, there are still some nails and bits of shingle in the gravel. I'll rake again this weekend.

Called Patricia at the insurance office to ask about the premium. She said the renewal notice went out last week and I should have it by Saturday. She also said the roof replacement might qualify for a small discount on the homeowners policy, but I'd need to send them the final invoice. I told her I'd mail it. She said I could also just drop it off.

2024-05-03
Friday. Warm. The renewal notice came in the mail. Premium is going up again, $1,872.00 for the year, due by 5/31. That's about $90 more than last year. I called Patricia to ask if the roof discount had been applied. She said not yet, that she needs the invoice first. I told her I'd bring it in on Monday.

Also noticed the gutters are pulling away from the house a little at the back corner, by the downspout. I'll have to get someone to look at that. I don't want water getting behind the fascia.

2024-05-04
Saturday. Sunny. I spent the morning cleaning out the gutters on the front of the house. They were full of leaves and some of that black grit from the old shingles. The back ones I left for now, since the corner is loose and I don't want to pull on it.

Mr. Chen across the street asked how the roof turned out. I told him it looks good and the crew did a clean job. He said he might need his roof done next year.

2024-05-05
Sunday. Cloudy. I didn't do much. Went through my folder to make sure I have copies of everything for the insurance discount. I have the signed contract, the final invoice from Dale, and the receipt for the last payment. That should be enough.

Reminder: drop off invoice at the insurance office Monday.

2024-05-06
Monday. Cooler. I went to the insurance office after work and gave Patricia the final invoice from Dale. She made a copy and gave me the original back. She said the discount will be applied to the renewal, and I should get a revised notice in a few days. She also said if the premium still looks wrong after that, to call her directly.

2024-05-07
Tuesday. Windy. Revised renewal notice came in the mail. The premium is now $1,798.00, so the roof discount saved me $74. I'll pay it before the end of the month. I wrote myself a note to mail the check by 5/28 so it gets there before the due date.

2024-05-08
Wednesday. I noticed the loose gutter again when I got home. The corner by the downspout is sagging more than I thought. I called Dale to ask if he knows anyone who does gutters. He said he doesn't, but he recommended a guy named Ray who does siding and gutters. He gave me the number. I'll call him tomorrow.

2024-05-09
Thursday. Called Ray. He said he can come by Saturday morning to look at the gutter and give me an estimate. He said he also does siding if I ever need it. I told him it's just the gutter for now.

2024-05-10
Friday. Paid the insurance renewal. Wrote a check for $1,798.00 and mailed it this morning, certified. I want a record that it got there.

2024-05-11
Saturday. Ray came by at 9:30. He looked at the back corner of the house and said the gutter is pulling away because a couple of the hangers have worked loose. He said it's an easy fix, he can reattach it and add a few extra hangers for about $120. I said go ahead. He'll come back next Saturday to do the work.

Description of Loss:
On the evening of February 5, 2024, a severe thunderstorm passed through the Dripping Springs area. The storm produced large hail and high winds. documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
2023-10-18
Rained all morning. Good, the ground needed it. Found a small leak in the laundry room ceiling, right corner near the vent. Dripping into a bucket now. Could be the roof, could be the vent pipe flashing. Called a roofer, guy named Mike from Apex Roofing. He's coming Friday to take a look. Need to clear the stuff out from under the window in the laundry room so he can get to it. Also, the leak is right above the water heater. Hope that's not a problem.

2023-10-19
Still overcast. Called the insurance agent about the roof leak. She said get a roofer's report first, then call her back. She gave me the claim number to jot down: CLM-2023-4471. Told me to take photos of the stain and the bucket. Did that. Also took a photo of the ceiling around the stain. The bucket is at 2 inches of water after 24 hours. Not a gusher, but steady.

- Photos on phone in folder "leak Oct 2023".
- Claim number CLM-2023-4471.
- Mike from Apex coming Fri 10/21, 9:30 AM.

2023-10-20
Cleared the laundry room. Moved the dryer vent hose so there's a path. Also put an old towel down to catch drips when I empty the bucket. Paid the water bill online. Confirmation #88421. The leak is still dripping. Called Mike to confirm tomorrow. He said he'd bring his ladder and a moisture meter.

2023-10-21
Mike came at 9:30 sharp. Went up on the roof. Found the problem – the boot around the vent pipe is cracked and the flashing is pulled up about an inch on the north side. He said it's an easy fix, maybe $350 for parts and labor. He sealed it temporarily with some caulk to stop the leak for now. Took photos of the boot and flashing. He'll email me a formal estimate Monday. The bucket hasn't caught a drop since he left, so fingers crossed.

- Mike's estimate due via email ~10/24.
- Temporary seal should hold until then.

Delgado Residence street address 4102 Mockingbird Lane. Record status: current.

2023-10-22
Sunny and cool. The leak is dry. Put the laundry room back together except for the bucket, which I'll leave until the real fix is done. Went to HEB, got the WD-40. Fixed the back gate hinge. Quiet now. Also bought a new pack of rags. Need to call the insurance agent Monday with Mike's estimate. She wanted the roofer's report before we talk about coverage.

2023-10-23
Monday. Mike's email came in at 8:15 AM. Estimate is $380 total: $150 for the boot, $150 for flashing repair, $80 for labor. Itemized, looks fine. Called the insurance agent, left a voicemail with the estimate amount and the claim number. She said she'd call back after she reviews it. Also, the neighborhood fall cleanup is Nov 4. Checked the flyer – they do take latex paint, but not oil. Good, the shed cans are latex. Will drop them off.

2023-10-24
Agent called back. She said the claim is open, and since the damage is from a storm (there was a hail storm back in April, remember?), it might be covered. She needs the photos and the estimate. Sent them via email. She said a claims adjuster might need to come out to verify the damage. Waiting to hear. Also, the bucket is still dry. Mike's temporary fix is holding well.

- Photos sent to agent 10/24.
- Awaiting adjuster visit.

2023-10-25
No word from the adjuster yet. Called the agent, she said they're backed up but should schedule within a week. Fine. Meanwhile, the weather is nice. Raked the back yard today. Got 4 more bags. Put them behind the fence with the others. That's 10 total now. Monday pickup should handle it.

2023-10-26
Thought I heard dripping in the laundry room, but it was just the water heater cycling. The ceiling stain is dry. Touched it – no dampness. Good. Spent some time cleaning the garage. Found the old paint cans – 3 cans of latex, all sealed. Good to go for Nov 4. Also found an old box of holiday decorations from last year. Noted to go through it before the season starts.

documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
- Photos sent to agent 11:15 AM.
- New claim opened, linked to April claim.
- Wait for adjuster call.

2024-02-04
Sunday. No call from the adjuster yet. The agent did email back at 3:10 PM confirming she received the photos and the claim is in the system. She said the adjuster is scheduled for tomorrow or Tuesday, depending on the storm backlog. Noted. Meanwhile, went outside and inspected the shed more closely. The dent is about the size of my fist, on the lower back corner, and it looks like the paint chipped around the dent. Will need to patch that to prevent rust. Also checked the gutters – one seam on the front corner looks like it might be separating. Not sure if that's from the hail or just old age. Took a photo anyway and added it to the claim notes. The fence picket is still on the ground. Will pick it up before mowing. The weather is sunny and cold today, in the 40s. Good day to stay inside.

- Check gutters – front seam, possible separation.
- Shed dent: fist-sized, paint chipped.
- Fence picket still down.

Storm Date event date 2024-02-03. Record status: current.

2024-02-05
Monday. Adjuster called at 8:50 AM. A man named David, he said he'd be out this afternoon between 1 and 4. I said fine. He asked about the April leak and whether the roof boot was repaired. I told him yes, Mike fixed it in October, and I have the receipt. He said to have it ready. He also asked about the shed. I told him about the dent and the chipped paint. He said he'd look at it. While waiting, I swept the hail off the back patio – there was still a pile in the corner. Also picked up the fence picket and leaned it against the garage. At 1:20 PM David arrived. He walked around the house, took a lot of photos. He climbed up on the roof with a ladder he had in his truck. He was up there maybe 20 minutes. He said the roof shingles have some granule loss in a few spots, and a couple of shingles on the south slope look like they might have been lifted by the wind. He said the AC fins are definitely dented and he'd note that. He looked at the shed and said the dent is minor but the paint chip needs sealing to avoid rust. He also looked at the gutter seam and said it might be from the hail, but he'd need to check if the seam was already weak. He said he'd write up the report tonight and send it to the agent tomorrow. I gave him Mike's receipt for the boot repair. He said that would help with the April claim. He left at 2:40 PM. I felt good about it, but I'll wait for the report.

- Adjuster visit done 2/5, report expected 2/6.
- Roof: granule loss, possible shingle lift.
- AC fins dented.
- Shed dent minor, paint chip.
- Gutter seam questionable.

2024-02-06
Tuesday. No report yet. Checked email at 9:00 AM – nothing. Called the agent at 10:15 AM. She said David's report is still being written and should be in by the end of the day. She said I'd get a copy by email. Fine. Meanwhile, I went to the hardware store and got a small can of rust-preventive paint for the shed dent. It's the same color as the shed, or close enough. Will patch it tomorrow when the weather is dry. Also picked up a new nail for the fence picket. Might just reattach it myself instead of waiting. The weather is clear and cold. Good day for errands. Checked the laundry room bucket one more time – still dry. The boot fix is solid. Noted to follow up on the report tomorrow if I don't hear back by 5 PM.

- Follow up on report if no email by 5 PM 2/7.
- Shed paint patch planned for 2/7.

documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
The report says the hail size he used in his assessment was 2.75 inch max. That matches what I remember from the storm – it was the biggest I've seen in the 12 years I've lived here. The report lists it as the storm's max hail size. Good to have that in writing.

I called the agent at 4:00 PM to confirm she got it. She said yes, and that she'd file the claim with the ins. company tomorrow morning. She said the claim number would be assigned within a day or two. She also said I should get quotes from contractors for the roof work, but to wait for the ins. adjuster's estimate before signing anything. Noted.

- Report received 2/7, 47 photos.
- Hail size max 2.75 inch in storm description.
- Claim to be filed 2/8.
- Get contractor quotes, but don't sign until ins. estimate arrives.

2024-02-08
Thursday. The agent called at 11:00 AM. Claim filed. Claim number: CLM-2024-01874. She read it to me over the phone and said I'd get an email confirmation too. She said the ins. company will assign their own adjuster to do a damage assessment. That could take a week or more, depending on how busy they are. She said to expect a call from them to schedule a visit. I wrote the claim number on a sticky note and put it on the fridge.

After lunch I called three roofing companies for estimates. First one, Peak Roofing, said they could come out next Tuesday. Second one, Summit Exteriors, said Thursday. Third one, Blue Ridge Roofing, said they'd have to check their schedule and call me back. I left my number. I'll give them until Monday.

Also called an HVAC place about the AC fins. The guy I talked to, Ron, said they do free estimates for hail damage. He said he could come by Monday afternoon. I scheduled it for 1:00 PM. He said to have the adjuster's report handy. I'll print a copy.

The shed paint is dry. Looks fine. Not perfect, but it'll keep the rust from starting. I'll touch it up again in the spring.

Storm Date hail size max 2.75 inch. Record status: current.

- Claim # CLM-2024-01874
- Peak Roofing – Tue
- Summit Exteriors – Thu
- HVAC (Ron) – Mon 1:00 PM
- Blue Ridge Roofing – call back pending

2024-02-09
Friday. No call from Blue Ridge yet. I'll try them again Monday.

The ins. company's adjuster called at 10:00 AM. Her name is Patricia Okafor. She said she handles the northern part of the county. She asked if she could come out next Wednesday, Feb 14, in the morning. I said yes. She said she'd be here between 9 and 11. She asked me to have any receipts for temporary repairs ready. I mentioned the boot repair and the shed paint. She said to keep the receipts for the paint too, since it's a preventive measure. Good. I have both.

She also asked if I had any photos of the storm damage from the day of. I said yes, I took some on my phone while David was here. She said to email them to her before the visit. I'll do that tonight.

After the call, I went to the bank to deposit a check from my sister. Not related to the claim, just life. While I was there, I noticed the ATM receipt printed wrong – it was missing the last two digits of the deposit amount. I went inside and the teller fixed it. Not a big deal, but I like to keep my records straight.

- Ins. adjuster visit: Wed 2/14, 9-11 AM.
- Email photos to P. Okafor before then.
- Keep receipts for boot repair and shed paint.

2024-02-10
Saturday. Cold but sunny. I spent the morning going through my photos from the storm and picking the best ones for Patricia. I sent her 12 photos by email at 11:30 AM. I wrote a short note explaining what each one showed – the roof from the street, the dented AC fins, the shed, the gutter seam, and a couple of the hail itself on the patio before I swept it. She replied within the hour, said she got them and they'd help.

documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
I showed her the folder with the receipts. She looked at the boot repair and the shed paint. She said both were reasonable temporary repairs. She asked if I had a receipt for the tarp from the first night. I said no, I bought it at the hardware store and paid cash, didn't think to keep the receipt. She said that's fine, she can note it as an expense if I can find any record. I'll check my bank statement; I might have used my debit card. I thought I paid cash, but I'm not sure now.

She said the dented AC fins are "cosmetic" but she'll include them in the report anyway. She said the gutter seam at the corner of the garage is a separate issue from the hail, and the adjuster's report will note it as "pre-existing wear." I didn't argue. She said the final report should be ready in 5 to 7 business days. She'll email me a copy.

I sent her a thank-you email after she left. She replied right away, said to call her if I have questions.

- P. Okafor – visit done. Report expected in 5-7 business days.
- Check bank statement for tarp purchase.

2024-02-15
Thursday. Summit Exteriors came by at 10:00. Two guys, one older and one younger. The older one, Mike, did most of the talking. He walked the roof, took measurements, looked at the attic from the hatch in the hallway. He said the ventilation looks fine, which is good. He said the shingles are at the end of their life and the hail damage is "moderate." He quoted me $9,400 for a full tear-off and replacement with architectural shingles. He said that includes new underlayment and ice and water shield at the eaves. He left me a printed estimate with a line-item breakdown.

I asked about a metal roof. He said they don't do metal, they're strictly asphalt. He said if I want a metal roof, I should call a different company. Fine.

He said they're booking about 3 weeks out. If I decide to go with them, they need a 20% deposit to hold the date. I told him I'm still waiting on the insurance report, so I can't decide anything yet. He said no problem, the estimate is good for 90 days.

Maya R. Delgado's email address is maya.delgado@example.com. Record status: current.

- Summit Exteriors – estimate $9,400. Good for 90 days.
- Still waiting on Blue Ridge call-back.

2024-02-16
Friday. No call from Blue Ridge. I'm starting to think they don't want the job. I called them again this afternoon. The same woman answered. She said Dale is out sick and will call me Monday. We'll see.

I also checked my bank statement online for the tarp. Turns out I did use my debit card. The transaction is there, $24.37 at the hardware store on Feb 3. I printed the statement page and added it to the folder. I'll email that to Patricia too, just to be thorough.

I spent the evening looking at the Summit estimate. The line items make sense. The price is a little higher than I hoped, but not crazy. I called Peak Roofing to confirm their visit for Tuesday. The woman who answered said they'll be here between 9 and 12. She asked if I had a chance to look at their website. I said no. She said they have photos of recent jobs. I said I'd look.

- Blue Ridge – Dale out sick, call Monday.
- Tarp receipt found – sent to P. Okafor.
- Peak Roofing – Tue 2/20, 9-12.

2024-02-17
Saturday. Cold and windy. I didn't do much. I looked at Peak's website. Their photos look good. They have a few jobs in the area. I saw one that matched my roof style. I'll ask about it on Tuesday.

I also looked at the Summit estimate again. The line items are:
- Tear-off and haul-away: $2,100
- New underlayment: $900
- Ice and water shield (eaves and valleys): $600
- Architectural shingles (30-year): $3,800
- Ridge vent and caps: $500
- Labor: $1,500
- Total: $9,400

documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
2024-04-01
Monday. Rain this morning, cleared by noon. Dale from Blue Ridge called at 9:15 to confirm. He said they can start on the 8th, weather permitting. I told him the check from the insurance company came in the mail on Saturday. He said they'll need the deposit before they order materials, so I should drop it off this week. I said I'd bring it by Wednesday.

Called Patricia Okafor this afternoon to tell her the check arrived. She said good, and that she'd already sent the final report to the carrier. She asked if I had the contractor's certificate of insurance. I said I'd get it from Dale. She said to email it to her once I have it, so she can close the file.

- Blue Ridge start date: Mon 4/8, weather permitting
- Deposit due before materials order
- Need COI from Dale → email to P. Okafor

2024-04-02
Tuesday. Sunny, cool. Went to Blue Ridge's office after work. Dale wasn't there, but the receptionist took my deposit check. She gave me a receipt and a copy of their certificate of insurance. I looked at it in the car—it's current through October. I emailed the PDF to Patricia when I got home.

Also stopped at the bank to deposit the insurance check. The teller asked if I wanted it held. I said no, just deposit it. It should clear in a couple days. I'll pay the rest of the balance when the work is done.

- Deposit paid: $1,880 (20% of $9,400)
- COI emailed to P. Okafor
- Insurance check deposited

2024-04-03
Wednesday. Windy. Dale called to say the shingles are in stock and they'll deliver them Friday. He said they'll do the tear-off on Monday, then the underlayment and ice and water shield on Tuesday, and the shingles Wednesday and Thursday. He said the ridge vent gets done on Friday. That's if the weather holds.

I asked about the old skylight. He said they'll frame it out and patch the decking, but they won't install a new one. I said that's fine, I don't need one. He said the patch will be covered by the new shingles and you won't be able to tell it was there.

- Shingle delivery: Fri 4/5
- Tear-off: Mon 4/8
- Underlayment + ice/water: Tue 4/9
- Shingles: Wed 4/10 – Thu 4/11
- Ridge vent: Fri 4/12

2024-04-04
Thursday. Warm for April. I cleared the driveway and moved the car to the street. I also took down the wind chimes by the front door so they don't get in the way. The tarp is still on the roof from February. Dale said they'll take it down when they start the tear-off.

I looked at my folder to make sure I have everything. I have the original estimate, the signed contract, the deposit receipt, the COI, and the insurance paperwork. Patricia said the adjuster's report is final, so I don't need to worry about that anymore.

The neighbor across the street, Mr. Chen, came over to ask about the noise. I told him the roof work starts Monday. He said he'd let his wife know. He asked how long it would take. I said about a week, maybe a little more if it rains.

2024-04-05
Friday. Overcast. The shingles were delivered this morning. Two pallets in the driveway, wrapped in plastic. Dale came by with the delivery to check the order. He said everything looks right. He also brought the dump trailer and parked it in the driveway, so the old shingles will go straight in.

I asked him about the weather for Monday. He said the forecast is clear, so they'll start at 7:30. He said they'll be done with the tear-off by the end of the day, unless they hit plywood that needs replacing. He said he'd call me if that happens.

- Shingles delivered
- Dump trailer in driveway
- Start time: Mon 7:30 AM

2024-04-06
Saturday. Nice day. I stayed home in case anyone came by. Nobody did. I looked at the pallets from the window. They're still wrapped. I read the contract again to check the payment schedule. It says the balance is due upon completion. Good.

documents.title: Personal Journal of Maya Delgado
documents.content:
2024-05-01
Wednesday. Rain off and on all day. The roof is done and I'm still getting used to how quiet the house is without the tarp flapping. Dale came by this morning to pick up the last check. I had it ready. He walked around the house first, checked the ridge vent and the flashing around the chimney, then said everything looked good. I gave him the final payment of $4,150.00. He said the warranty paperwork will be mailed to me within a week. I put the receipt in the folder.

2024-05-02
Thursday. Clear. I finally took the wind chimes back out and hung them by the front door. Also swept the driveway, there are still some nails and bits of shingle in the gravel. I'll rake again this weekend.

Called Patricia at the insurance office to ask about the premium. She said the renewal notice went out last week and I should have it by Saturday. She also said the roof replacement might qualify for a small discount on the homeowners policy, but I'd need to send them the final invoice. I told her I'd mail it. She said I could also just drop it off.

2024-05-03
Friday. Warm. The renewal notice came in the mail. Premium is going up again, $1,872.00 for the year, due by 5/31. That's about $90 more than last year. I called Patricia to ask if the roof discount had been applied. She said not yet, that she needs the invoice first. I told her I'd bring it in on Monday.

Also noticed the gutters are pulling away from the house a little at the back corner, by the downspout. I'll have to get someone to look at that. I don't want water getting behind the fascia.

2024-05-04
Saturday. Sunny. I spent the morning cleaning out the gutters on the front of the house. They were full of leaves and some of that black grit from the old shingles. The back ones I left for now, since the corner is loose and I don't want to pull on it.

Mr. Chen across the street asked how the roof turned out. I told him it looks good and the crew did a clean job. He said he might need his roof done next year.

2024-05-05
Sunday. Cloudy. I didn't do much. Went through my folder to make sure I have copies of everything for the insurance discount. I have the signed contract, the final invoice from Dale, and the receipt for the last payment. That should be enough.

Reminder: drop off invoice at the insurance office Monday.

2024-05-06
Monday. Cooler. I went to the insurance office after work and gave Patricia the final invoice from Dale. She made a copy and gave me the original back. She said the discount will be applied to the renewal, and I should get a revised notice in a few days. She also said if the premium still looks wrong after that, to call her directly.

2024-05-07
Tuesday. Windy. Revised renewal notice came in the mail. The premium is now $1,798.00, so the roof discount saved me $74. I'll pay it before the end of the month. I wrote myself a note to mail the check by 5/28 so it gets there before the due date.

2024-05-08
Wednesday. I noticed the loose gutter again when I got home. The corner by the downspout is sagging more than I thought. I called Dale to ask if he knows anyone who does gutters. He said he doesn't, but he recommended a guy named Ray who does siding and gutters. He gave me the number. I'll call him tomorrow.

2024-05-09
Thursday. Called Ray. He said he can come by Saturday morning to look at the gutter and give me an estimate. He said he also does siding if I ever need it. I told him it's just the gutter for now.

2024-05-10
Friday. Paid the insurance renewal. Wrote a check for $1,798.00 and mailed it this morning, certified. I want a record that it got there.

2024-05-11
Saturday. Ray came by at 9:30. He looked at the back corner of the house and said the gutter is pulling away because a couple of the hangers have worked loose. He said it's an easy fix, he can reattach it and add a few extra hangers for about $120. I said go ahead. He'll come back next Saturday to do the work.
